members.title: Ex-Air Force officer Tahsif’s death: Friend Dwip taken into police custody
members.lead: Police have taken Dwip, a younger friend of former Air Force officer KM Tahsif Souri, 28, into custody in connection with Tahsif’s death. The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) took him into custody. Dwip was taken from a house in the capital’s Mohammadpur area late on Thursday night. Md Abu Yusuf, superintendent of police, for PBI’s Law and Media wing, confirmed the information on Friday morning. .Ex-Air Force officer’s body recovered from Turag River. Abu Yusuf said Dwip had been taken to the PBI Metro North office in connection with Tahsif’s death. As the two had gone out and were together on the night before the incident, Dwip would be questioned about it, he said. The information he provided would be checked and verified. Tahsif left his home in Uttara, in the capital, on Tuesday evening. At 1.35 am that night, he sent his mother a voice message on her mobile phone saying he was on his way home. However, he never returned. Police recovered his body from the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon. His relatives said the motorcycle he had taken with him when he left home was also missing. .Ex-Air Force officer Tahsif identified through mobile phone found with body. Before Tahsif went missing, CCTV footage showed him with a man. Family members identified the man as Dwip. The footage shows Tahsif meeting the man in front of a garage at the Rajuk Uttara Apartment Project in Sector 18 of Uttara on Tuesday night. After shaking hands, the two left on separate motorcycles. Tahsif’s father, KM Eneyetul Karim, told Prothom Alo that in the evening on the day of the incident, Dwip, a younger friend of Tahsif’s, came downstairs to call him. Tahsif went down, saying he would speak to Dwip and return. He never came back home. .Ex-Air Force officer’s body recovered: Home minister declines to comment for now. members.title: Motorcycle recovered near Turag river; police checking whether it belonged to Tahsif
members.lead: A motorcycle has been found in an area near the spot on the Turag River in Dhaka where the floating body of former Air Force officer KM Tahsif Souri, 28, was recovered. The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) recovered the motorcycle late Thursday night. The agency said it was found in the Mazar Basti area of Tongi, about 50 yards from the spot where the body was recovered. PBI officials said the Rajbari Ghat area is known as a drug hotspot. They suspect Tahsif may have fallen into the river and drowned while fleeing drug traders. . Mohammad Abu Yusuf, special superintendent of police at the Law and Media Wing of PBI headquarters, told Prothom Alo this morning, Friday, that investigators were checking whether the recovered motorcycle belonged to Tahsif. However, their preliminary assessment was that it was likely his. The recovered motorcycle has been taken to Uttarkhan Police Station in the capital. PBI is assisting the River Police in investigating the incident. Tahsif left his home in Uttara in the capital on Tuesday evening. At 1:35 am that night, he sent his mother a voice message on her mobile phone saying he was returning home. But he never came back. .Ex-Air Force officer Tahsif’s death: Friend Dwip taken into police custody. The next afternoon, Wednesday, the River Police recovered Tahsif’s body from the Turag River near Rajabari Ghat in the Uttarkhan Police Station area. Tahsif had taken his motorcycle with him when he left home. After his body was recovered, his family said they could not find the motorcycle. PBI has now said that a motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar Basti area of Tongi, near Rajabari Ghat. Before Tahsif went missing, CCTV footage showed him with a man.
